text:
Jalen Chatfield scored against Edmonton on Nov 21, his third goal of the season, and then played 22:54 at Madison Square Garden the next afternoon. That second number is the story: the undrafted defenseman, a Stanley Cup winner with Carolina last spring, is a top-four regular on the best team in the East.

His pair with Jaccob Slavin has played 375 minutes at five on five and taken 56% of the expected goals, outscoring opponents 16-10. Carolina takes about 55% of the chances with him on overall, though the team is better without him, which is the usual caveat for someone who plays next to an elite partner.

Evolving-Hockey made the same point last season: he plays with strong teammates (99th percentile), and opponents got more chances with him on. The goals are a little lucky too, three on 1.3 expected.

What to watch: how his minutes hold up when the playoff race tightens. Carolina's projected point total is 120, so the stress test is probably months away.
